title: Trillium Labs opens nonprofit AI lab to publish the training methods frontier models keep closed
key_facts: Trillium Labs launched as a nonprofit AI research lab, co-founded by researcher Nathan Lambert and Tom Zick.
It plans to publish complete post-training recipes: data, code, evaluations and intermediate checkpoints.
Post-training is the stage after initial training in which developers shape a model's behaviour and capabilities.
It argues frontier labs have published less detail as commercial value grew.
Nonprofit status lets it publish failed experiments and run controlled studies without protecting IP.
Backers so far are Halcyon Futures and Schmidt Sciences; it is seeking more funding and computing resources.
Advisors named: Thomas Wolf, Hanna Hajishirzi, Graham Neubig and Bryan Catanzaro; offices in the SF Bay Area and Cambridge, Massachusetts.
quote_evidence: A handful of closed research programs cannot provide the diversity of questions, methods, and perspectives that a technology this consequential needs.
The lab says its nonprofit structure will allow it to publish failed experiments as well as successful ones
Trillium has begun with support from Halcyon Futures and Schmidt Sciences
why_it_matters_hint: Outside researchers could study how frontier-style models are shaped.
notes: Based on Trillium's own statements and Lambert's LinkedIn post; no output yet.
